findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — [P2, confidence 75, advisory] With two external issues from the same integration linked to one Sentry group, `if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id:` suppresses propagation to the second issue when the first changes assignee, leaving that customer’s linked issues inconsistent; the strongest rebuttal is that integration-wide suppression intentionally prevents echoes, but the second issue is a distinct destination already supported by the outbound GroupLink fanout, so preserving the originating external issue key and excluding only that issue prevents the echo without deleting valid synchronization edges.

tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:221 — [P2, confidence 100, advisory] For users synchronizing an issue across two integrations, `mock_sync_assignee_outbound.assert_not_called()` with only a matching integration and manually supplied `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` accepts a regression that suppresses every sourced assignment and bypasses verification that inbound assign/deassign attaches provenance; although the existing source-free outbound tests and inbound database assertions verify ordinary assignment, they never assert propagation from integration A to B while excluding A, so add that scenario for both assignment and deassignment to protect the changed behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — [P2, confidence 75, advisory] With two external issues from the same integration linked to one Sentry group, `if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id:` suppresses propagation to the second issue when the first changes assignee, leaving that customer’s linked issues inconsistent; the strongest rebuttal is that integration-wide suppression intentionally prevents echoes, but the second issue is a distinct destination already supported by the outbound GroupLink fanout, so preserving the originating external issue key and excluding only that issue prevents the echo without deleting valid synchronization edges.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the diff. Looking at the code at line 390, when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`, the method returns False, blocking ALL outbound sync to that integration. However, the sync_group_assignee_outbound function in sync.py iterates over ALL external_issue_ids linked to a group via GroupLink. If a single Sentry group has multiple external issues linked from the same integration (e.g., two Jira tickets), and one of those tickets triggers an inbound assignment change, the current logic would block syncing to ALL issues from that integration, including the second ticket that should legitimately receive the update. The fix should track the specific external_issue_id that originated the change, not just the integration_id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:221 — [P2, confidence 100, advisory] For users synchronizing an issue across two integrations, `mock_sync_assignee_outbound.assert_not_called()` with only a matching integration and manually supplied `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` accepts a regression that suppresses every sourced assignment and bypasses verification that inbound assign/deassign attaches provenance; although the existing source-free outbound tests and inbound database assertions verify ordinary assignment, they never assert propagation from integration A to B while excluding A, so add that scenario for both assignment and deassignment to protect the changed behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a gap in test coverage. The diff adds logic to prevent sync cycles (integration A -> A), but the tests only verify: 1) outbound sync with no source, 2) outbound sync blocked when source matches target integration. There's no test verifying that when integration A triggers an assignment, it still propagates to integration B (a different integration). The test at line 221 only tests the blocking case, not the pass-through case for different integrations. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for the new sync-cycle prevention logic.
